text:
B: Hiya! Can you hear me okay?
A: Yeah, fine. Craig. You alright?
B: Gemma. I'm good thanks, last one of the round. Is that a Leigh scarf on your shelf?
A: It is, yeah. And you've got a Warriors magnet on your fridge, so this could go badly.
B: Oh, it could. I'm from Wigan, my dad'd disown me if I was nice to you.
A: I'm in Leigh, so we're practically neighbours. Sorry.
B: Ha. Lily's dad lives in Leigh, actually, so I'm over there every other Friday dropping her off.
A: Small world. What do you do?
B: Primary teacher. Year 4. You?
A: Instrument tech at a water treatment works near Warrington. Sensors, control panels, that sort of thing. I'm on call this week, so fingers crossed.
B: Oh, the engineer lady, Carys, she'd love you. She does flooding.
A: Yeah, she'd be one of the sensible ones I reckon.
B: She was lovely. So have you got kids? I'm guessing from the pram there.
A: Ruby, she's four. Starts reception in September. Is there anything I should know? You're a teacher.
B: Honestly, get her doing her own coat and shoes. Zips, buttons, all that. And put her name in everything, because thirty jumpers all look the same by October.
A: Coat and shoes. That's doable. Leanne'll be pleased I asked.
B: And don't worry if she cries the first week. They're usually fine five minutes after you've gone. It's the parents who come out in bits. I was a mess with our Lily, and I'm a teacher, I should've known better.
A: Yeah, I reckon that'll be me.
B: Do you do anything in the evenings, when you're not getting called out?
A: Five-a-side, Wednesdays. We were short again last week.
B: I do netball Tuesdays. Goal defence. We lose every week but we have a laugh.
A: That's the main thing.
B: The lad from Birmingham had never heard of a pie barm, by the way. And Carys called it a bap.
A: The Wolves lad called it a bap and all. I had to have words.
B: Finally, somebody normal! I have one every Friday.
A: Saturday morning for me, from the bakery.
B: Meat and potato?
A: Is there another kind?
B: See, we can be friends. Just not on derby day.
A: Not on derby day. That's fair, that.
